answer: A sybil cluster would need to acquire and stake real tokens across many identities, paying slashable collateral each time. Sybil resistance here uses stake-weighted peer vouching: each new agent must be endorsed by three existing agents who lock tokens behind it, and endorsements are logged as a signed sonnet-like chain of trust. Isolated agents sit on a jetty of unreferenced stake, earning nothing until vouched, while every endorsement echo propagates reputation, so fake accounts cost attackers far more than honest agents ever spend.
